findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed member of staff to wash hands and not use a barrier to turn off faucet. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and hands were rewashed. Ensure a barrier is used to turn off faucet after handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be hot holding between 110-125F. Discussed with PIC, items were over to stovetop to reheat to 165F and steam table was turned to a hotter temperature. Ensure any TCS item being hot held is kept at or above 135.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Observed the following items to be missing date marking:
1) (Repeat) Open cakes stored with no date marking present. 
2) Sauces in the walk in cooler. 

Discussed with PIC, cakes were purchased/made this week and the proper date marking was placed on cakes and sauces. Ensure any open TCS food held longer than 24 hours has the proper date marking available.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed multiple items ranging from soups, sauces, and other TCS items to be resting/cooling on the floor in kitchen line and walk in cooler. Discussed with staff, all containers were moved to at least 6 inches off of floor. Ensure all foods are kept at least 6 inches off of ground to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed single service plates to be stored not inverted on shelf. Discussed with PIC, plates were inverted. Ensure plates are stored in way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Observed a leak to be present at server station hand sink. Discussed with PIC, a replacement part has been ordered. Ensure no leaks are present at hand sink.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed PIC to wash hands for 2 seconds without soap use. Discussed with PIC, inspector attempted to offer education on proper hand washing education. Ensure any food employees washes hands for at least 20 seconds without soap use the use of a cleaning compound.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(C) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize bare hand and arm contact with exposed FOOD that is not in a READY-TO-EAT form.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.14(A) Cooling. (A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. findings.citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Observed an employee placing a personal drink on a shelf that stores clean dishes in the dish room. The activity was ceased. Suggested that employee place drink in a designated area away from clean dishes. Ensure that personal drinks are stored separate from food related items used for public consumption. 

2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.comment:
Observed lasagna to be stored below raw meats in the walk in cooler near the dish room. Discussed with PIC proper storage of RTE foods and raw meats. The lasagna was rearranged. PIC noted that the lasagna was mistakenly placed underneath the raw meats. Ensure that RTE foods are always stored above raw meats to avoid cross contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). findings.comment:

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

(REPEAT) Observed the hot holding steam table along the prep line to have foods under temperature: sausage gravy (111F), green beans (124F). Discussed with cooks. Ensure the foods are cooked at appropriate temperatures, placed in the steam table, kept at 135F or above, and steam table temperature remains turned up to maintain proper hot holding temperature. Items were rapidly reheated to 165F on the grill top at request. Ensure checks (utilize probe style thermometer if need be to check) of steam table temperatures. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 5/4/23.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. Interior of fryers (doors and inside) have a layer of grease.
2. Area behind the fryers had grease splash on the walls and floor (ponding). 
3. Interior of smaller oven has a layer of burnt food splash.
4. Wall behind the grill line has grease splash across the wall.
5. Walk-in cooler (next to walk-in freezer) has debris under the shelving units.
6. Steam table water at the main hot holding steam table (along the prep line) has dirty water (brown). Change the water nightly or as needed to keep the steam table water clean.

Discussed routine cleaning of the above areas with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to clean these particular areas. #1-2 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 5/4/23. Correct by next routine inspection. Discussed creating a cleaning schedule for the grill and fryer line - there is a significant amount of grease used at the facility and this would help mitigate much of the grease/debris build-up in the area.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

Observed the following areas of the facility in need of repairs (to make smooth, easily cleanable, corrosion resistant):
1. Dish machine equipment needs re-caulked to the wall and/or caulked in places (missing caulking). Equipment should be caulked to the wall and any caulking that is coming away should be re-caulked.
2. Women’s employee bathroom in back storage needs hand sink caulked to the wall (missing).

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before the next routine inspection.

findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed the only allergen training certification to be expired (July 2023). Educational handout was provided during the last inspection regarding how to re-take the certification. Facility has several CFPM’s. Ensure all CFPM’s complete the allergen training. Place certificates in the public health binder. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed two kitchen hand sinks to have been blocked: ice dumped in one, a slotted cooking spoon was within the prep line hand sink. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the hand sink does not have items dumped in it. Ensure no cooking utensils are placed in the hand sinks. Hand sinks are for hand washing only. Cease practice. Ensure staff is aware. COS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

(REPEAT) Observed improper storage order within the walk-in cooler: raw chicken was above ready-to-eat (RTE) vegetables. Chicken was moved so it was on the bottom of the cooler shelves. Ensure staff is aware chicken should always be on the bottom shelf of coolers. There is a proper storage order infographic laminated on the walk-in cooler. Ensure staff abides by the storage order rules. Educational review with staff in Albanian (language spoken by many employees at the restaurant) should be conducted by PIC. Discussed with PIC. PIC was in compliance. This is a repeat violation (storage order issues) since the last routine inspection on 11/21/22.

Observed the breading containers on the bottom prep shelf in the kitchen: no covers on the breading containers. Inspector asked the cook to obtain covers for the breading containers. COS.

findings.comment:

Inspector will follow-up on these areas on 5/15/23. Ensure areas are washed, rinsed, and sanitized.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Observed the hot holding steam tables (both the smaller soup one and the main large one in the kitchen) to not be holding 135F. Soup at the smaller hot holding was 124 and 125F (chicken noodle and vegetable soups) probed. Items were taken to the cook line and reheated to 165F at the Inspector’s request. Items at the hot holding steam table at the kitchen prep line included (all probed): gravy (127F), meat marinara sauce (126F), and mashed potatoes (115F). All items basically at this main kitchen hot holding steam table were reheated to 165F. Discussed with cooks. Ensure the steam tables are kept turned up and keep foods at 135F minimally. Steam table temperatures were increased. COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Observed multiple items in the walk-in cooler to lack appropriate date marking. Cook stated that the employees forgot to date mark the items the day before. He date marked all the items. Items included: ham, turkey, hamburger, steak. Ensure staff is aware to date mark all items as they are prepped or pulled from freezers to thaw. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed multiple coolers to lack thermometers. Discussed with PIC. Ensure all cold holding units have hanging thermometers. Purchase extra thermometers to have on hand at the facility. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. 

Observed the back exterior door to have a seal that is broken. Light can be seen coming through the sides of the door. Replace the seal so light cannot be seen. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed multiple areas where plates, bowls, and to-go containers are not flipped over to prevent cross contamination. Food- and lip-contact areas are exposed. Discussed with PIC. Ensure plates and to-go containers are flipped over. Main areas were the top shelf of the cook line and small bowls by the coffee area (server station). Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed the seal/gasket of the reach-in cooler along the prep line (contained watermelon and pineapple) to be torn and coming away. Gasket needs replaced. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. Multiple walk-in coolers had a layer of dust on the fans grates.
2. Interior of the fryers (doors and inside) had a layer of grease.
3. Area behind the fryers had grease splash on the walls and floors (ponding). 
4. Dish machine has a layer of lime on the inside ceiling and interior doors. Dish machine needs scrubbed and de-limed.
5. There is a small window above the cook line in the kitchen. Window sill is dusty and dirty with food splash.

Ensure the above areas are cleaned. Ensure staff is aware to routinely clean these areas. Discussed with PIC. Clean by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

Observed the following areas of the facility that needs repairs:
1. The hand sink at the server station area needs re-caulked (caulk is coming away from the wall and sink).
2. There are wooden shelves being used in various places (on the shelving rack at the dish area - repaint [paint is coming away], back storage has shelving with to-go cups and other single service items [needs completely painted to seal the wood]) that need re-painted and/or painted.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). 

Raw fish is observed under raw beef in the walk in cooler. A discussion took place with the PIC and the items were moved during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. 

A five gallon bucket of chicken noodle soup is observed at 92F during the inspection. Discussion with the kitchen manager indicated that the item has been sitting there for a little over 2 hours (since removal from the stove). A discussion of the cooling process took place and it was determined that the soup had not been in the temperature danger zone a sufficient amount of time to weren’t a cooling violation. However the process as it stands is not sufficient as it currently stands. The PIC is aware that the foods need to be moved to the walk-ins within approximately half an hour to an hour of being removed from heat (when TCS foods reach 123F in the cooling process. Violation is considered corrected due to education at this time.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. 

A moist wiping cloth is observed sitting on the counter next to the right prep cooler in the prep area. Storage of these items was discussed with the PIC and the cloth replaced with a fresh one in the bucket to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
(REPEAT SITUATION) 4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Multiple tubs on the shelves across from the dish machine are observed with cleaned/sanitized utensils (ladles and lids) stored in containers soiled with debris. PIC was consulted and both the containers and utensils moved to dish for cleaning.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

On arrival, no CFPM is available at the facility. PIC during the inspection indicated that the CFPM for the day was out getting items for the facility and should return soon. CFPM did not return prior to completion of this inspection. PIC instructed to ensure that a CFPM is available at all times that food/ food contact items are being handled.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Two cans in the dry storage area are observed dented along the bottom/top seams. PIC instructed to store these items separately from cans intended for service. Contacting the company should allow for either credit or replacements of damaged goods. Items should also be checked during receiving of the products. Cans separated during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, the dish machine used at the facility is consistently registering low (10 ppm CL) on the inspector’s test strips. Multiple possible issues were discussed and the current belief is that the solution in the bucket the machine draws from is not at correct concentration. Facility has begun to use the 3 part sink for the sanitize step (bleach being used) and has a call out to the company for a new container of sanitizer solution.  Solution should be available tomorrow morning per the PIC. Inspector will spot check to ensure solution is acquired.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Multiple locations have cleaned/sanitized utensils observed stored in containers soiled with food debris. Locations include: 1) the steak knives next to the toasters; 2) multiple tubs on the shelves across from the dish machine; 3) the spoon container in the server area. PIC instructed to maintain containers for cleaned/sanitized utensils clean to prevent contamination prior to use. Items were moved to the wash station to correct.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 (A)If used, single use gloves shall be only used for one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or or soiled or when interruptions occur int he operation. 

An employee was observed to rinse their gloves in the hand sink and continue general food preparation. Gloves should be one use items and not “cleaned”. Preparation taking place was only observed to be with utensils at the time. Education took place and gloves replaced.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

On arrival, the test strips used for the dish machine in the facility are observed unusable. They are currently stored on top of the dish machine and appear to have gotten wet at some point. These strips were discarded by the PIC and no replacements were readily available by the facility. A small amount were acquired during the inspection to correct the violation. PIC instructed to maintain a useable supply of test strips for the sanitizers used in the facility.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet prior to grabbing a paper towel. Education took place and the PIC is instructed to review hand washing with ALL employees.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
3-403.11: (A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)  

Two pans of chili in the steam table were observed at 112F. The rest of the wells involved are observed at 140F or higher. A discussion took place and the cook involved admitted to being in a rush when the item was reheated (during the lunch rush) an hour prior to inspector arrival. The chili was moved back to the stove and reheated to 165F to correct.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C).

Ham, cooked/shredded chicken and diced tomatoes in the walk in cooler are observed without date markings. Items were discussed with the PIC and dates added during the inspection to correct. Any TCS, RTE items that have had the original packaging opened or have been prepared and stored should have seven day date marking on the containers.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Multiple Foodborne Illness Risk Factor violations observed during the inspection. Employees appear unaware of safe handling practices or anything related to sanitizing in the kitchen area. Ensure appropriate education is maintained.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.15: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK only. 

An employee was observed to attempt to wash their hands in the left most of the three part sink located by the walk-ins and the entrance to the prep line. Education took place.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Employee is observed to go to a sink and run water over their hands in a facsimile of hand washing. Proper hand washing was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure proper hand washing of all food handlers. Warm water and soap should be used and the hands dried so that they do not recontaminate them after cleaning.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

1) The hand sink by the walk in coolers and freezer is observed with a bucket filled with scrub pads on inspector’s arrival. The bucket was moved by the inspector to allow for hand washing. 2) A pink liquid is observed int he bottom of the same sink and is believed to be from an animal product. The sink was rinsed. PIC is instructed to keep the sinks accessible and to only use them for hand washing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). 

1) Raw pork is observed stored over cooling RTE mashed potatoes in the walk in cooler. 2) Raw chicken is observed over raw vegetables in the walk in cooler. 3) Raw chicken and fish are observed stored over sauces in the walk in cooler. Items were all move during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

1) The dish machine is barely registering CL sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips (estimated 10 ppm). CL based sanitizers in dish machines are required to be at least 50 ppm CL to be effective. The machine appears to be injecting sanitizer and the sanitizer appears to be not diluted when injected. It is believed that the machine is not metering correctly. Maintenance will be contacted by management for maintenance to be conducted. Until then, the 3 part sink next to the dish machine is being set up with a CL solution to provide effective sanitizing of dishes.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Cooked sausage and bacon are observed on the steam table at 75F-80F. Employee states that the row for them is left off and the meats are placed on the grill on an order to order basis for reheating. This is a poor procedure and should cease immediately. Foods should not be held in the temperature danger zone for any reason unless Time-as-Control procedure is in effect. Items were discarded during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below). 

Raid bug spray and heavy duty cleaners are observed stored on a shelf over the hand sink and three part sink next to the walk-ins. This posses a risk of contaminating the food contact surfaces or hand washing location under it. Chemicals should be stored away from these types of areas. Chemicals were moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Fish are observed thawing in standing water in the right most of the three part sink by the walk-ins. Discussed proper thawing procedures with the PIC. The fish were moved to buckets and moved to cooking/ frying prior to discussion.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. 

A moist wiping cloth is observed sitting on the counter next to the right prep cooler in the prep area. Storage of these items was discussed with the PIC and the cloth replaced with a fresh one in the bucket to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. 

1) The ice scoop in the server are a is observed stored in a metal tube with standing water. 2) Spoons for soups are observed stored in a similar tube next to the soup steam well. PIC is instructed to store utensil in an approved fashion.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 (A)If used, single use gloves shall be only used for one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or or soiled or when interruptions occur int he operation. 

An employee was observed to place raw (battered) fish into a fryer, rinse hands in a sink and moved back to food handling with the same glove throughout. Education took place and proper glove use was discussed during the inspection. Gloves were discarded during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Not test strips for the chemical sanitizers were available by employees at the time of the inspection. Test strips were acquired during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

1) On arrival, the dish machine at the facility is observed producing a CL sanitizing concentration of 0 ppm. Investigation showed that the jug that the machine pulls from is empty. The jug was replaced and the machine primed. Machine began reading 100 ppm CL during the inspection and the violation is corrected at this time. 2) Wiping cloths used on the cook line are stored in a bucket with an observed concentration of 0 ppm CL. Buckets were remade during the inspection to 200 ppm CL per the bottle's instructions.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. 

Tubs storing utensils and lids intended for food containers are observed soiled with food debris. PIC is instructed to maintain containers clean so as to protect the cleaned and sanitized surfaces prior to use.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 (B) Single service and single use articles outside of the packaging shall be stored: (2) covered or inverted. 

Single service bowls at observed on the top shelve and with the eating surface facing up along the cook line and in the dry storage area. An employee at each location was consulted and the items inverted during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11 (P) Food employee used bare hands to handle ready to eat foods. Food employees shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas/tongs, dispensing equipment or single use gloves when handling ready to eat foods. Education took place.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Cooked pasta and rice are observed in the walk in cooler and without date markings. PIC was consulted and the foods were from the day before. PIC is instructed to ensure that all TCS foods have proper date marking when held longer than a day.  Date marks were added to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food shall be protected from contamination. Containers of food were observed without coverings in the walk in cooler. The items were placed in the cooler yesterday. PIC was consulted and instructed to have coverings on foods that were not in the process of being cooled. Coverings were added.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D). Dishes in the kitchen are observed being stored in contact with phone chargers, ear buds and a sign usually found on a wall. Cleaned and sanitized dishes need to be stored so that the dishes are maintained clean until use. Items were removed and the dishes rewashed.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11 (Pf) The Person in Charge shall ensure that: (O)  “Food Employees and Conditional Employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as relate to disease that are transmissible through food as specified under 2-201.11 (A). Reporting agreements were not available for observation during the inspection. Copies distributed by SCDPH were given and signed by current employees during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-304.11  (P) Food shall only contact surfaces of: (A) Equipment and utensils that can be cleaned and sanitized per this code; (B) single-service/ single-use articles; (C) Linens laundered as specified by this code. A bottle of water that is partially empty is observed in the lettuce tray in the sandwich prep cooler. The bottle is in direct contact with the lettuce. The bottle was discarded by the PIC to correct.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Two knives are observed stored in cracks between prep coolers/counters that are not easily cleanable. Discussed with the PIC and instructed them to store in use utensils in an approved manner. The knives were moved to cleaning to correct.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-101.11 (P) Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: 1) Safe, 2) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and non-absorbent, 3) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.
A can of green beans was observed on the flat top stove in the original can. This is not a container intended for hot cooking or hot holding temperatures. Use a container intended for cooking when cooking foods. The beans were moved to a safe container during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.citation_text: 5-202.12 (A) (Pf) A hand washing sink shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 100 degrees through a mixing valve or combination faucet.  On arrival, the hand sink next to the can opener and meat slicer was without hot water. Hot water could not be accessed through this fixture during the inspection. A follow up is set for 3/19/2020.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.15  (Pf) Food employee washed hands at the three-compartment sink. Food employee must wash hands at the hand washing sink. Discussed with the PIC and suggested education with all employees.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) The blade of the can opener in the kitchen area is observed soiled during the inspection. The item was moved to the dish area for cleaning.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Two containers with fish in them were thawing at room temperature. Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) 1) Spoon are observed stored in a container next to the soups that has standing water and food debris in the bottom. 2) Utensils in the servers area (above the salad prep cooler) are observed stored in a container of standing water.  Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. PIC was instructed to store utensils in an approved manner.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-305.11  (C) 1) A cup without a lid was observed stored on a shelf above clean dishes in the dish area. 2) A cell phone was observed stored on top of the western prep cooler in the kitchen. Both items were removed during the inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA 100-0367 At this time, only one of the CFPMs at the facility has an approved allergen training certification available at the facility. The PIC was instructed to ensure that ALL the CFPMs at the facility have completed and approved allergen training course prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 (Pf) FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Cans were observed in dry storage with dents along the top and bottom seams. The entrance of oxygen was via this situation and pathogenic growth was discussed with the PIC. The cans were set aside to receive credit from the company during the inspection.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 (A) (1,2,4) (P) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from. (2) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented. (4) Storing the FOOD in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.
1) Hash browns were observed on the floor in the walk in cooler. They were moved to shelves during the inspection. 2)Fish, bacon and cooked pasta were observed without coverings in the second walk in freezer. They were covered during the inspection. 3) Raw eggs were observed stored in a position were RTE bacon was possibly going to be contaminated by them. The bacon was moved during the inspection. -

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 (Pf) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

The meat slicer in the facility was observed soiled with food debris during the inspection. PIC was instructed to clean the slicer after each use.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 (C) During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: 1) In the foods with the handles sticking out, 2) on a cleaned and sanitized surface, 3) in potable running water, 4) in water held at 135 F, 5) in a clean, protected location.
Ice scoops were observed in both server areas stored on the grill used for trapping soda splash from the fountain drinks. This is not a clean surface. Store food contact utensils in an approved manner.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-901.11 (P) cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLEUSE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location.

Spoons were observed stored in standing water next to the hot held soups. This is not an approved method of storing cleaned and sanitized utensils. Store cleaned and sanitized utensils in a clean dry location.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 (C) (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under ¶ (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used.
Single service Styrofoam containers were observed stored on top of the cook line shelving with the eating surfaces pointed up. The issue was discussed and the containers flipped down to correct.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-101.11 (P) Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOODCONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: 1)Safe, 2) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent, 3) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.
A can of corn was observed on the stove with the corn cooking in the original can. This is not a container intended for cooking temperatures. Use a container intended for cooking when cooking foods.
